messages:
From: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@mediview.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mediview Security <security@mediview.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T14:08:00Z
Subject: Questions after today's demo - storage/retention specifics

Thanks for the demo today — it was helpful. A few follow-ups from our security and engineering teams so we can move forward with procurement: 

1) For the interactive chat flow we saw, what exactly is persisted? Do you store raw prompts, final model outputs, intermediate tokens, or only anonymized metadata?
2) Where is persisted data stored geographically for the hosted product (region/REPLICATION)? Can we request a US-only residency?
3) Retention windows: what are your default TTLs for (a) prompt inputs, (b) model outputs, and (c) debug logs/traces? Can they be shortened?
4) Access controls & encryption: KMS integration? Customer-managed keys?
5) Evidence: would you share the latest SOC 2 report and a short summary doc that maps these items to our control framework?

We need answers and any artifacts by EOD tomorrow (2026-11-24) to keep the procurement timeline.

- Emma
Emma Lawson
Senior Product Security Manager | Mediview Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lawson <emma.lawson@mediview.com>
Cc: Mediview Security <security@mediview.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T16:12:00Z
Subject: RE: Questions after today's demo - storage/retention specifics

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. I'm capturing answers below and will follow up with internal confirm and two artifacts attached (retention summary + SOC 2 redacted). Short answers first, then details per item.

Short answers (high level):
- Persisted items: by default we persist prompt inputs (encrypted) and request/response logs for 30 days; model-generated outputs are persisted for 7 days for troubleshooting unless configured otherwise; intermediate token-level data is not stored beyond ephemeral runtime unless debug mode is enabled.
- Residency: Hosted runs in multiple regions; we can scope a tenant to US-only (us-west-2 us-east-1) for data at rest and logging.
- TTLs: Defaults are 30d (inputs), 7d (outputs), 365d (audit/traces). Shortening to customer-requested lower bounds is possible on Dedicated or Private; hosted allows some TTL overrides for enterprise plans.
- Encryption/KMS: Customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS supported for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we offer both Redwood-managed and customer-managed KMS options (region-dependent).
- Evidence: attaching redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf and our SOC 2 Type II (redacted) as soc2-report-2026.pdf.

I'll loop in Aditya (product) and Karthik (security) internally to validate exact wording for the artifacts and confirm the replication/residency mechanics. If you need a formal attestation matrix against your control IDs, we can produce it next week.

Next steps: 1) I'll confirm the exact S3 buckets/regions and TTL override path with Aditya by tomorrow morning. 2) If you need US-only residency hard requirement, we can scope that into the contract and flag as part of Dedicated capacity discussion.

— Priya
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T18:03:00Z
Subject: Internal: confirm storage buckets, retention defaults, KMS options for Mediview (MV-2026-089)

Aditya/Karthik — quick internal: Mediview asked for exact persistence semantics and evidence; I drafted the reply above and attached artifacts. Can you confirm the specifics below so I can finalize before EOD tomorrow: 

1) Hosted default storage: are prompt inputs stored in s3 with 256-bit AES at rest in region selected by tenant? Which exact buckets/prefixes are used for request logs vs. model outputs?
2) TTL enforcement: we apply an automated lifecycle that deletes objects older than default TTLs (30/7/365). Are there known exceptions (long-term diagnostic exports, audit exports)?
3) KMS: Hosted supports Redwood-managed keys in all regions; customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS is available for dedicated tenants in us-west-2/us-east-1. Are we also supporting customer-managed CMKs for hosted tenants in the coming quarter?
4) Residency: For hosted US-only, does our replication avoid cross-region backups? Confirm retention of logs in US only when tenant flagged.

If you can reply inline with confirmations or edits, I'll incorporate and send final to Emma.

Thanks — Priya
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:17:00Z
Subject: RE: Internal: confirm storage buckets, retention defaults, KMS options for Mediview (MV-2026-089)

Priya — confirmed below, please send to Emma: 

1) Storage & what is persisted:
- Prompt inputs: persisted by default to encrypted S3 in tenant region (us-east-1 or us-west-2 for US-only tenants). Objects stored under s3://redwood-hosted/tenants/{tenant-id}/requests/ (JSON payloads).
- Model outputs: persisted to s3://redwood-hosted/tenants/{tenant-id}/responses/ by default for 7 days; these are primarily for diagnostics and streaming replay.
- Intermediate tokens: not persisted beyond runtime unless debug_mode=true for a session; debug-mode storage is opt-in and flagged in the tenancy config.
- Metadata/observability: request IDs, timing, and sampling-based traces persist up to 365 days in audit logs stored in separate logging buckets with stricter access controls.

2) TTL enforcement & exceptions:
- Lifecycle policies enforce deletion at the object level after the configured TTL (S3 lifecycle rule). Exceptions: we do allow scheduled export snapshots for diagnostics or compliance (exported to long-term archive) only with explicit customer approval and documented justification.

3) KMS & keys:
- Redwood-managed KMS: default for hosted; AES-256 for object encryption + envelope encryption with AWS KMS.
- Customer-managed keys (CMKs): supported for Dedicated and Private immediately; hosted will support CMKs in targeted regions (us-east-1/us-west-2) starting H1-2027 via a phased rollout. For Mediview procurement, we can scope CMK support as part of Dedicated capacity or a hosted-enterprise addendum.

4) Residency & replication:
- For US-only tenancy flag: control plane and data plane avoid cross-region replication; backups and logs remain in the selected US region(s). Cross-region DR exists but is opt-in and requires contract-level approval.

Artifacts: redwood-data-retention-summary.pdf (summary mapping to your control categories) and a redacted soc2-report-2026.pdf are attached. For a formal control matrix (mapping to Mediview control IDs) we'll produce a CSV next week.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference
